title: Unnormalized isomorphism of algebraic relative dualizing objects
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a flat finitely presented homomorphism of commutative Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Put $B=A\otimes_RA$, with coprojection $p_1:A\to B$, $a\mapsto a\otimes1$, and let $A$ be a $B$-module via multiplication. Let $M,N\in D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] be pseudo-coherent over $A$ [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Assume each has finite Tor amplitude over $R$, meaning that for $T=M,N$ there are integers $a_T\le b_T$ such that $H^i(T\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q)=0$ for every $R$-module $Q$ and $i\notin[a_T,b_T]$. Compute derived tensor using flat resolutions and derived Hom using injective resolutions, as in [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on the one-point ringed site. Suppose $R\operatorname{Hom}_B(A,M\otimes_{A,p_1}^{\mathbf L}B)$ and $R\operatorname{Hom}_B(A,N\otimes_{A,p_1}^{\mathbf L}B)$ are each isomorphic to $A$ in $D(B)$. Then there exists an isomorphism $M\cong N$ in $D(A)$. No choice of diagonal generator and no compatibility with a chosen generator is part of this conclusion.

source.place: Tag 0E2D, lemma-uniqueness-relative-dualizing, using Definition 0E2C, definition-relative-dualizing-complex; the Noetherian special case.

proof.text: The source's $R$-perfect condition is exactly the two displayed assumptions on each $T=M,N$: Definition 0DHS says pseudo-coherent over $A$ and finite Tor dimension over $R$, and the latter means a single finite Tor interval valid for every $R$-module. No finite Tor dimension over $A$ or $B$ follows or is used. Taking $Q=R$ in the hypothesis shows that $T$ has bounded cohomology. Since $A$ is Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-pseudocoherent-cohomology-criterion] gives finite generation of every $H^i(T)$ from pseudo-coherence. Thus $M,N\in D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(A)$.

source.place: Tags 0DHS and 066E. Expanded-hypothesis equivalence and bounded coherence.

proof.text: Choose a finite polynomial presentation $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$, which exists by finite presentation. Set $C=R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,P)[n]$ with its coinduced $A$-action. Apply [lem-trf-algebraic-shriek-relative-perfect]: the map is flat and finite type and both rings are Noetherian, so $C\in D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(A)$ and its scalar-action morphism $h:A\to R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,C)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0BZW, parts (1)(a)--(c), polynomial relative dualizing complex.

proof.text: For each $T=M,N$ apply [lem-trf-polynomial-diagonal-rhom-reduction] to the same presentation $P$. All its hypotheses are exactly Step 1 and the given flat finite presentation. Restrict the assumed isomorphism $R\operatorname{Hom}_B(A,T\otimes_{A,p_1}^{\mathbf L}B)\cong A$ along the actual coprojection $p_1:A\to B$. Its target becomes $A$ with its usual action, since multiplication composed with $p_1$ is the identity. The reduction therefore gives an isomorphism $g_T:A\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,T)$ in $D(A)$. This uses restriction of scalars only; no underived restriction along $B\to A$ or $p_2$ identification is asserted.

source.place: Polynomial-diagonal tensor-Hom reduction, derived in report.md from Tags 068X, 07VI, 0A65 and 0A6A.

proof.text: Use the tensor-Hom adjunction of [lem-pod-projective-hom-evaluation-model] with a bounded-above projective representative of $C$ (its pseudo-coherence supplies one by Step 2). Let $f_T:C=C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A\to T$ be the adjunct of $g_T$. The scalar map $h$ is the adjunct of $\mathrm{id}_C$. Naturality of adjunction gives $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,f_T)\circ h=g_T$: both sides are adjunct to $f_T$ under the same adjunction. Since $h$ and $g_T$ are isomorphisms, $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,f_T)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0A65, derived internal-Hom adjunction; adjunct of the identity is scalar action.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-semidualizing-rhom-conservative] to $C$ and $f_T:C\to T$. Step 2 verifies bounded finite cohomology and the scalar-action isomorphism for $C$; Step 1 verifies bounded finite cohomology of $T$; Step 4 verifies that derived Hom sends $f_T$ to an isomorphism. Thus both $f_M:C\to M$ and $f_N:C\to N$ are isomorphisms. The composite $f_N\circ f_M^{-1}:M\to N$ proves the assertion. The choices of $g_T$ were arbitrary; no normalized comparison is concluded.
